topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture by framing its themes, connecting them to prior histopathology practicals, and outlining the learning outcomes.

topics.label: Viral Origins and Laboratory Assays of Cellular Transformation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the historical discovery of tumor viruses, the identification of cellular proto-oncogenes captured by retroviruses, and the experimental assays used to measure cellular transformation.

topics.label: Classification and Functional Mechanisms of Oncogenes and Tumor Suppressors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the major classes of cancer-driving mutations and explain how dominant, recessive, and dominant-negative mechanisms operate within cell cycle regulatory pathways.

topics.label: Mechanisms and Consequences of Genetic Instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish between sequence and chromosomal instability and describe the specific repair, replication, and mitotic segregation defects that produce them in cancer cells.

topics.label: Multistep Tumor Progression and Hereditary Cancer Predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the stepwise model of mutation accumulation in tumorigenesis, examining how inherited germline mutations and subsequent evolutionary dynamics influence tumor development.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Recommendations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the session by summarizing the coverage of learning outcomes, recommending supplementary reading, and previewing upcoming lecture content.
